title: Brown's work in the B-2 and Floyd Odlum's funding

tellings.quote: In fact, Floyd Odlam, who is the majority owner of Northrup, who funded Brown's work in the 60s, paid Brown 4,000 bucks or I don't remember, 2,000 bucks 4,000 bucks a month, his family uh uh the same amount uh until until he died.

plain: Michels says a businessman named Floyd Odlum, whom he calls the majority owner of the aircraft maker Northrop, funded the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown's work in the 1960s and paid Brown about 2,000 or 4,000 dollars a month (Michels does not remember which), and then paid Brown's family the same amount until he died. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of a story that links Brown's work to Northrop's B-2 stealth bomber. If true, it would mean a major aircraft company kept quietly backing Brown's research for decades.
